clues.q: This South African DJ's 2019 gospel-house hit “Jerusalema,” featuring Nomcebo Zikode, sparked a worldwide dance challenge in 2020.
This Nigerian singer had a breakout Afropop hit in 2014 with “Johnny,” about a boyfriend with too many girlfriends.
Growing out of Congolese rumba, this fast, guitar-driven dance music takes its name from a French verb meaning “to shake.”
This band of Tuareg guitarists from northern Mali won the 2012 Grammy for Best World Music Album for “Tassili.”
This Ethiopian vibraphonist and bandleader is known as the father of Ethio-jazz.
Viola Davis leads the all-female Agojie warriors of the Kingdom of Dahomey in this 2022 film.
This 2016 Disney film starring Lupita Nyong'o tells the true story of Phiona Mutesi, a chess prodigy from Kampala, Uganda.
This South African comedian, author of the memoir “Born a Crime,” hosted “The Daily Show” from 2015 to 2022.
Directed by and starring Genevieve Nnaji, this 2018 film was Nigeria's 2019 Oscar submission but was disqualified for having mostly English dialogue.
Souleymane Cissé's 1987 Malian film about a young man with magical powers won the Jury Prize at Cannes.
The famous painted limestone bust of this Egyptian queen, wife of Akhenaten, is displayed in Berlin.
Ancient Egyptians wrote on sheets made from this tall reed that grew along the Nile.
Hero of an epic still sung by griots, this “Lion King” founded the Mali Empire in the 13th century.
Named after a village in central Nigeria, this ancient culture is famous for its terracotta sculptures of human heads.
This 25th Dynasty Kushite pharaoh is mentioned in the Hebrew Bible and was buried in a pyramid at Nuri.
Crowned in 1930, this Ethiopian emperor was born Tafari Makonnen.
In 2018, the Kingdom of Swaziland officially changed its name to this.
In 1990, this leader of the independence movement SWAPO became Namibia's first president.
In 1960, this charismatic independence leader became the first prime minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Botswana's first president, his marriage to Englishwoman Ruth Williams inspired the 2016 film “A United Kingdom.”
Woven in narrow strips by Ghana's Asante and Ewe weavers, this brightly patterned cloth is worn for celebrations and graduations.
This long, loose hooded robe with full sleeves is traditional dress for men and women in Morocco.
The shúkà cloth worn by the Maasai of Kenya and Tanzania is best known in which color?
Often worn with a conical mokorotlo hat, this woolen wrap is a proud symbol of Lesotho.
This printed cotton cloth from the Swahili coast, sold in pairs, usually carries a proverb or saying along its border.
Nicknamed “the Mother City,” this South African city sits at the foot of Table Mountain.
Famous for its ancient medina and leather tanneries, this Moroccan city gave its name to a brimless red felt hat.
Tanzania's largest city, its Arabic name means “haven of peace.”
Facing Brazzaville across the Congo River, this city is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
This Eritrean capital became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017 for its early 20th-century modernist architecture.

questions.q: Sea between Egypt and Saudi Arabia?
Animal called the “ship of the desert”?

clues.q: His 2004 love song “African Queen” made this Nigerian singer, born Innocent Idibia, a star across the continent.
clues.hint: His stage name starts with a number.

clues.q: This Tanzanian bongo flava superstar founded the record label WCB Wasafi.
clues.hint: His stage name pairs a gem with a precious metal.

clues.q: Nicknamed “the Lion of Zimbabwe,” this musician pioneered chimurenga music built on mbira patterns.
clues.hint: His first name is also a biblical apostle's.

clues.q: Leader of the band TPOK Jazz, this Congolese rumba giant was nicknamed “the Sorcerer of the Guitar.”
clues.hint: Known by a single name that sounds Spanish.

clues.q: Rooted in spiritual healing ceremonies, this Moroccan music is played with a three-string guembri and metal castanets called qraqeb.
clues.hint: Celebrated each year at a festival in Essaouira.

clues.q: Lupita Nyong'o played both a mother and her sinister double in this 2019 Jordan Peele horror film.
clues.hint: A two-letter title.

clues.q: Pearl Thusi starred as a South African secret agent in this 2020 Netflix action series.
clues.hint: Named after the heroine.

clues.q: Michel Ocelot's 1998 animated film, drawn from West African folktales, follows a tiny, brave newborn who outwits the witch Karaba.
clues.a: What is Kirikou and the Sorceress?
clues.hint: Named after the little boy hero.

clues.q: Ousmane Sembène's 1966 debut feature follows a young Senegalese woman who moves to France to work for a family.
clues.a: What is Black Girl (La Noire de…)?
clues.hint: Its English title has two words.

clues.q: Held in Ouagadougou since 1969, this pan-African film festival awards the Golden Stallion of Yennenga.
clues.hint: Known by a seven-letter French acronym.

clues.q: Ancient Egyptians preserved the dead through this process, removing organs, drying the body with natron and wrapping it in linen.
clues.hint: The result might later appear in a museum case.

clues.q: Often called the first named architect in history, he designed the Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara.
clues.hint: Later revered as a god of medicine.

clues.q: This bishop of Hippo, in what is now Algeria, wrote “Confessions” and “The City of God” around 400 CE.
clues.hint: A Florida city is named after him.

clues.q: Famous for a small golden rhinoceros found in a royal grave, this hilltop kingdom near the Limpopo River flourished around 1200 CE.
clues.hint: Its site lies where South Africa meets Botswana and Zimbabwe.

clues.q: Hatshepsut sent a celebrated trading expedition to this land, source of incense, myrrh and ebony, recorded on her temple walls.
clues.a: What is the Land of Punt?
clues.hint: A four-letter name, probably on the Red Sea coast.

clues.q: The droning buzz of this long plastic horn filled stadiums during the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa.
clues.hint: Fans blow into it like a trumpet.

clues.q: In 1957, this lawyer and independence leader became the first president of the Republic of Tunisia.
clues.hint: His first name means “beloved” in Arabic.

clues.q: Known for waving a white handkerchief, he served as Zambia's first president from 1964 to 1991.
clues.hint: Often called “KK.”

clues.q: From 1971 to 1997, the Democratic Republic of the Congo was officially known by which name?
clues.hint: Derived from an old local name for the Congo River.

clues.q: A celebrated poet and co-founder of the Négritude movement, he served as Senegal's first president from 1960 to 1980.
clues.hint: The first African elected to the Académie française.

clues.q: Completed in 1993 on Casablanca's waterfront, this mosque partly built over the Atlantic has a towering minaret.
clues.a: What is the Hassan II Mosque?
clues.hint: Named after a Moroccan king.

clues.q: These brass plaques and sculptures were cast for the royal court of the Edo kingdom centered on today's Benin City, Nigeria.
clues.hint: Named after a metal alloy and the kingdom.

clues.q: A royal capital from the 1630s, this Ethiopian city is known for the castles of the Fasil Ghebbi enclosure.
clues.hint: Lies north of Lake Tana.

clues.q: This Ghanaian sculptor, long based in Nigeria, makes shimmering tapestry-like works from thousands of flattened bottle caps.
clues.hint: His name begins with a Spanish article.

clues.q: In 1991, this South African artist painted a BMW 525i Art Car with bold Ndebele patterns.
clues.hint: Her first name is shared with a biblical queen.

clues.q: This jackal-headed Egyptian god watched over embalming and guided the dead.
clues.hint: His head resembles a wild dog's.

clues.q: This clever spider is the trickster hero of countless Akan folktales from Ghana.
clues.hint: Also spelled with a K at the start.

clues.q: In Yoruba tradition, this fiery orisha, once a king of Oyo, rules thunder and lightning.
clues.hint: His symbol is a double-headed axe.

clues.q: According to the Ethiopian epic Kebra Nagast, this son of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba founded Ethiopia's royal line.
clues.hint: A later emperor took the same name as the second.

clues.q: In Egyptian belief, a dead person's heart was weighed against the feather of this goddess of truth and cosmic order.
clues.hint: A short name, often shown with an ostrich plume.

questions.q: Which river forms much of the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe?
Grande Comore, Mohéli and Anjouan are islands of which nation?
What is the currency of Egypt called?
The Blue Nile joins which other branch of the river at Khartoum? (Name its color.)
Mount Toubkal, North Africa's highest peak, rises in which mountain range?

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: Founded under Egypt's Ptolemaic dynasty, this legendary center of learning sought copies of every book it could obtain; a grand modern successor opened in the same city in 2002.
rounds.a: What is the Library of Alexandria?
rounds.hint: Located in a port city on the Mediterranean.
